  "title": "Improving newsletter signup flow",
  "body": "## Who's it for?\r\nUsers who want to subscribe to the newsletters\r\n\r\n## Problems to be solved\r\n- Our newsletter promo is currently getting a miniscule CTR from the `Sign up` button: Avg. 0.3% newsletters/session (See #2559 for full analysis)\r\n- Marketing want to increase the number of signups to What's On ([see their recommendations])(https://github.com/wellcometrust/wellcomecollection.org/issues/2703#issuecomment-558689254) \r\n- `/newsletter` page styling needs to be updated anyway as we're still on the old base page template\r\n\r\n## What does success look like?\r\n- Percentage of site visitors who signed up\r\n- Increase average monthly subscribers by 5%\r\n\r\nCompare v1 vs v2 usage against same period last year\r\n\r\n## Constraints\r\n- Timeboxed: Finish by Friday 17 January 2020\r\n- Avoid background patterns that are buggy in IE11/Edge\r\n\r\n## Where we can improve overall quality?\r\n- Eliminate bugs in IE11\r\n- Responsive design\r\n- Content improvements - wording\r\n- Decoupling from footer\r\n- Form elements\r\n- Design of newsletter page\r\n- Better integration with card system\r\n\r\n## Consider\r\n- Success and error states\r\n- Newsletter-specific differentiation\r\n- Brand elements from print assets\r\n- Form validation (that scales to other forms)\r\n- Degradation\r\n- Does it need to be situated at bottom of content above footer?\r\n\r\n## Decisions\r\n- Decided not to make it part of the footer because we may want an audience-specific newsletter to be promoted on relevant programme/activity pages\r\n\r\n## Testing\r\nWe'll AB test content of v2 : v2 (A) vs v2 (B)\r\n\r\n",

      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "That's our interpretation - not necessarily our Legal team's interpretation. I suggest we future-proof this (against impending GDPR audit) by following pattern that wellcome.ac.uk uses. I'm 80% certain that this will come up in the next few months."

      "id": 576306120,
      "url": "https://github.com/wellcomecollection/wellcomecollection.org/issues/2703#issuecomment-576306120",

      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "GDPR consent must be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous, by a clear affirmative action.\r\n\r\n> ‘consent’ of the data subject means any freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication of the data subject’s wishes by which he or she, by a statement or by a clear affirmative action, signifies agreement to the processing of personal data relating to him or her\r\n\r\nAll subscriptions are double opt-in, and as such the person entering an email address has to click the button that says, 'Yes, I want to receive email updates', under the paragraph, 'You've signed up to receive email updates from Wellcome Collection. Please confirm your subscription.' in a confirmation email they receive after form submission.\r\n\r\nAre we requiring users to consent to anything other than receiving the email itself. If not, then the clear affirmative action of clicking an unambiguous button seems good. \r\n\r\nIf we need them to have have read, understood, and agreed with our privacy notice before signing up, then there may still be a case for the checkbox with words to that effect.\r\n\r\n"
